title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #220
gist: Packy McCormick's weekly optimism roundup argues that SpaceX's orbital Starship catch makes full reusability real (marginal launch cost to ~$2-10M), highlights a 41%-mortality-reduction Phase 3 AML vaccine and a pancreatic cancer pill, Palmer Luckey's 1,000-year SLAB seastead, Tesla's Powercore solid-state transformer as evidence of two US industrial bases, and Earth AI's AI-found 3km copper-gold-PGM system. Extra Doses (Anthropic IPO, Google models, big AI rounds) are paywalled.

insights.claim: SpaceX caught an orbital Starship upper stage (Ship 42, Flight 15) with Mechazilla's chopsticks after it reached orbit, deployed Starlink satellites, and spent 22+ hours in space, completing the last major step toward rapid full reusability.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Removes the key technical risk to Starship's cost thesis; watch heat-shield durability and turnaround time as the next milestones.
insights.quote: Catching the orbital upper stage, the part that goes into orbit carrying the payload to complete a mission, was the final boss of rapid, full reusability. The final boss is dead.
insights.locator: (1) SpaceX’s Mechazilla Catches an Orbital Starship

insights.claim: With the Super Heavy booster (about 70% of Starship's cost) already reusable, the expendable upper stage was roughly 90% of Starship's marginal per-flight cost, imposing a $30-40M per-launch floor; reusing the upper stage cuts marginal launch cost to about $2-10M, or $20-100/kg versus Falcon 9's ~$1,000/kg internal cost.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A 10-50x drop in $/kg to orbit reprices every space business model (satellites, orbital data centers, in-space manufacturing).
insights.quote: the marginal cost of launch drops to something like $2-10M per launch, or $20-100/kg versus Falcon 9’s $1,000/kg internal cost
insights.locator: While the booster is more expensive at around 70%

insights.claim: SpaceX aims to fly about two Starships a week by end of 2027, hundreds per year by 2029, and multiple per day beyond that, carrying satellites, data centers and drug factories.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Launch cadence targets set the demand ramp for orbital data center and in-space pharma plays; track actual cadence against these dates.
insights.locator: SpaceX still has plenty of work ahead on heat-shield

insights.claim: SELLAS Life Sciences and Memorial Sloan Kettering reported positive Phase 3 REGAL results for galinpepimut-S (GPS), an AML immunotherapeutic vaccine: in 126 relapsed, transplant-ineligible patients in second-or-later remission, GPS alone delivered 24.0 months median overall survival versus 14.7 months for best available treatment, a 41% reduction in risk of death.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Positive pivotal data in a high-unmet-need population is a regulatory catalyst for SELLAS; AML has ~33% five-year survival and kills ~11,500 Americans a year.
insights.locator: (2) Leukemia Vaccine Cuts Risk of Death by 41%

insights.claim: GPS is an off-the-shelf peptide vaccine targeting WT1 rather than a personalized tumor-derived vaccine like Merck and Moderna's mRNA melanoma vaccine, which should make it faster, cheaper and more widely available, and WT1's presence in multiple blood cancers and solid tumors suggests possible label expansion beyond AML.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Off-the-shelf manufacturing plus multi-indication target potential improves commercial scalability versus bespoke cancer vaccines.
insights.locator: This isn’t the first promising vaccine this year.

insights.claim: Life-extending cancer therapies that are not cures still have option value: extra months of survival buy patients time for more permanent cures under development, so incremental survival gains compound as the therapy pipeline accelerates.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Frames incremental-survival drugs as both direct value and a bridge to future treatments, supporting sustained oncology investment.
insights.quote: an extra nine months both nine months and a call option on much longer
insights.locator: While it’s not a total cure

insights.claim: A new pancreatic cancer pill reported by the BBC shrank tumors to undetectable levels in one in 12 patients and halted tumor growth in 90% of 61 patients, with experts calling it the biggest pancreatic cancer breakthrough in decades, though durability is unknown.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Pancreatic cancer is among the hardest-to-drug cancers; early efficacy here signals a broader acceleration in oncology that investors should track.
insights.locator: (2a) Pancreatic cancer pill trial saw tumours vanish

insights.claim: 2026 has been an unusually strong year for cancer treatment readouts, and the author expects the pace of breakthroughs to continue.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Sentiment tailwind for oncology biotech as multiple Phase 3 wins stack up.
insights.locator: And if this year’s pace in cancer treatments

insights.claim: Palmer Luckey revealed SLAB, a privately funded offshore floating industrial seastead with a 1,000-year design life that he has been building since selling Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion in 2014, capitalized with friends at a $1 billion valuation.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A billionaire-backed bet on ocean platforms as industrial real estate; watch for capital raises and first operating tenants.

insights.claim: SLAB is designed to be cheaper than land and to operate outside the state and local regulations that the author and Luckey say cripple American heavy industry, targeting metal processing, desalination, oil refining, chemical engineering and frontier medical research.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Regulatory arbitrage via jurisdiction-free platforms is a new angle on US reindustrialization and permitting bottlenecks.
insights.quote: The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing
insights.locator: The idea is that SLAB will be a massive off-shore

themes.theme: Solid-state transformers and two US industrial bases

insights.claim: Tesla unveiled Powercore, a 7.4 MW solid-state transformer, adding another piece to the Musk companies' vertically integrated capability stack that removes a bottleneck for data center build-outs.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: SSTs speed up and cost down data center construction and may help stabilize the grid; Tesla's entry validates the category.

insights.claim: The author expects both Tesla and Heron Power (founded by ex-Tesla SVP Drew Baglino) to do well in solid-state transformers because demand is very large.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Tesla's entry is not framed as a threat to SST startups; demand supports multiple winners.
insights.quote: I think both Heron and Tesla will do well here. There is a ton of demand
insights.locator: We’ve talked about SSTs in the context of Heron Power

insights.claim: In the Electric Era, design leadership without manufacturing leadership is not a coherent strategy, and it becomes less coherent the better AI gets; Musk solves this by building nearly everything in-house, while a parallel American ecosystem is emerging to serve electric companies outside the Elonverse.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Favors vertically integrated hardware makers and the non-Musk supplier ecosystem; the US now has two modern industrial bases to invest across.
insights.quote: maintaining design leadership without manufacturing leadership is not a coherent strategic position, and one that gets less coherent the better you believe AI will get
insights.locator: There is a ton of demand, and as I wrote

insights.claim: The world spends roughly $14 billion a year searching for new mineral deposits, yet major discoveries have fallen about 70% over the past decade because easy deposits are exhausted, so new technology is needed to find harder deposits economically.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Electrification-driven metal demand meets declining discovery rates, creating a supply squeeze and an opening for exploration tech.
insights.locator: If those two parallel electric universes

insights.claim: Earth AI's Alpheus model reinterpreted 1969 and 1997 drilling data at Fontenoy/Meridian in New South Wales as a continuous magma-filled fault rather than scattered pockets, and 35 drill holes have since traced copper, gold, platinum-group metals and tungsten mineralization across 3km from 30m to 478m deep, with hints it may extend 8km.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Shows AI reprocessing of legacy exploration data can turn written-off sites into discoveries.
insights.locator: This week, the company announced that its Alpheus AI model

insights.claim: Earth AI owns its own drill rigs and labs, which let it start drilling five weeks after its model flagged Fontenoy and move toward feasibility faster than explorers relying on slow, expensive contractors.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Vertical integration compresses discovery-to-feasibility timelines, a key value driver for explorers.
insights.locator: Five weeks later, Earth AI started drilling

insights.claim: Earth AI, a not boring capital portfolio company, has 4,500 more targets flagged by Alpheus and could become a flywheel business in which proven discoveries are sold for cash that buys more rigs to prove out further targets, potentially doubling the world's mines.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Flywheel thesis for AI explorers; note the author's investor conflict (portfolio company).
insights.quote: I think the company has the potential to be one of the world’s most beautiful businesses
insights.locator: As we covered in our Deep Dive on Earth AI

themes.theme: AI acceleration and paywalled extra doses

insights.claim: The author reports that Anthropic is now public, with the paywalled section headlined as an Anthropic $1.5T IPO, alongside new Google models (Google Neon), a $5B Isomorphic Labs round, Science Corp's $400M, and Genesis AI's $500M for robot hands.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Signals extremely large AI capital-market events; details are behind the paywall so verify independently.
insights.locator: EXTRA DOSES: Science Breakthroughs, Anthropic $1.5T IPO

insights.claim: The author says almost every item in this week's Extra Doses would have made the top five as recently as three months earlier, implying the pace of breakthrough news is accelerating sharply.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Pace-of-progress sentiment marker from a widely read tech-optimist newsletter.
insights.quote: Almost everything in Extra Dose would have made the top 5 even like 3 months ago.
insights.locator: What a week to be alive.
